questions.question: position: absolute removes an element from normal flow and positions it relative to:

options.text: Its nearest positioned ancestor (or the viewport if none)

questions.explanation: absolute is offset from the nearest ancestor with position != static. Without one, it falls back to the initial containing block (viewport).

questions.question: position: fixed differs from absolute because it is relative to:
questions.explanation: fixed positions relative to the viewport and doesn't move on scroll (great for headers/modals).

questions.question: position: sticky behaves like:

options.text: relative until it would scroll past a threshold, then sticks like fixed within its parent

questions.explanation: sticky toggles between relative and fixed based on scroll position, constrained to its containing block — perfect for sticky headers.

questions.question: For position: absolute/relative/fixed, the offsets (top/right/bottom/left) are ignored when:
questions.explanation: top/left/etc. only apply to positioned elements (relative/absolute/fixed/sticky). With static they're ignored.

questions.question: z-index controls:

options.text: Stacking order of positioned elements (which appears on top)

questions.explanation: z-index sets paint order among positioned elements within the same stacking context; higher = closer to viewer.

questions.question: A 'stacking context' is created by, among others:

options.text: position + z-index, opacity < 1, transform, will-change, flex/grid child with z-index

questions.explanation: Many properties create a new stacking context (transform, opacity, position+z-index, will-change...), scoping z-index locally.

questions.question: To center an absolutely-positioned box both ways you use:
questions.explanation: Offset to 50% then translate back by half its own size — the classic absolute-centering technique.

questions.question: When is absolute positioning a poor choice?

options.text: For whole page layout (it breaks document flow and responsive behavior)

questions.explanation: Absolute positioning yanks elements from flow; using it for major layouts harms responsiveness. Flex/Grid are better for layout.
